# Reactions and prepared responses

## Reaction timing and monster reactions
A Reaction is an instant response to its stated trigger and may occur on the creature's turn or another's. It happens immediately after the trigger unless its description says otherwise; the interrupted turn then continues. After taking one, the creature cannot take another until the start of its next turn. Every creature can potentially make an Opportunity Attack, while a monster's additional reactions and their triggers appear in its stat block. Preserve the resource only when a likely later trigger better serves the shared objective.

## Opportunity Attacks
When a visible creature leaves the reactor's reach using its action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or one of its speeds, the reactor may spend its Reaction to make one melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike immediately before the creature leaves. Disengage prevents that movement from provoking. Forced movement and teleportation do not provoke under this trigger.

## Ready
Ready spends the action now to define a perceivable trigger and prepare either an action or movement up to Speed. Before the next turn, the creature may spend its Reaction immediately after the trigger or ignore it. A readied spell must normally take an action to cast, is cast and paid for when readied, and requires Concentration while held; if not released in time or Concentration breaks, it dissipates.
